faqs.question: What is a Raksha Bandhan wishes link?
faqs.answer: It is a single web address that opens a personalised greeting page built for one sibling, with their name, your photos and your message on it. You paste the URL into WhatsApp instead of pasting text. Nothing is installed at either end — it opens in the browser already on their phone.

faqs.question: How do I send a Raksha Bandhan wishes link on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Send one short line saying what it is and who it is from, then send the URL as the very next message on its own. A link appended to the end of a long wishes paragraph reads as a signature and gets skipped. Research in Nature Human Behaviour found around 75% of forwarded links are shared without anyone clicking them, so the framing line is doing real work.

faqs.question: Will my brother need an app to open the link?
faqs.answer: No. A wishes link opens as a normal web page in whatever browser is already on his phone. 51.1% of the 36,202 recorded opens on SubhSandesh happened on a phone, so the format is built around that assumption rather than a desktop one.

faqs.question: Can I put a password on a Raksha Bandhan wishes link?
faqs.answer: Yes, and set it before you share rather than after. 44.2% of SubhSandesh creators — 1,315 of 2,973 — password-protect a page before sending it. Send the password in a separate message from the link, because the two travelling together defeats the point.

faqs.question: Does the link expire after Raksha Bandhan?
faqs.answer: A URL has no expiry of its own, which is why the W3C's guidance on capability URLs says whoever granted access needs a route to revoke it. Practically, the password is your control rather than the calendar. Plan on the link outliving the festival, because it will.

faqs.question: Can I tell whether he actually opened the link?
faqs.answer: Views of shared pages are recorded — 36,202 so far, averaging 12.2 per page — so you can see that a page has been opened. Treat that as "somebody opened it", not proof of who: the same figure includes reopens and the page being shown to other people.

faqs.question: What if he forwards the link to the family group?
faqs.answer: Assume he might, because that is normal WhatsApp behaviour rather than a misuse. Part of the 12.2 average opens per page is exactly this. If there is an inside joke on the page you would not want read out, either cut it or set a password before sharing.

faqs.question: Is sending a link better than sending a rakhi wishes image?
faqs.answer: For something you spent an evening on, yes — an image gets one look and lands in a gallery, while a link stays addressable and averages 12.2 opens. For a one-line wish to a colleague, an image is fine and faster. The link earns its extra effort only when there is something worth reopening.

faqs.question: How early should I make the link for Raksha Bandhan 2027?
faqs.answer: Raksha Bandhan 2027 falls on Tuesday 17 August, so publish on the Monday evening. The median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 6.9 hours, so people keep tinkering far longer than they expect to and a same-morning build usually goes out unfinished.

faqs.question: Can I send the same link to more than one sibling?
faqs.answer: You can, but a page addressed to one person by name reads oddly to the second recipient. Make a separate page per sibling if the message is personal, and use one shared link only when the page is genuinely about the whole family.

faqs.question: What happens if I edit the page after sending the link?
faqs.answer: The URL stays the same and the page updates, so anyone reopening it sees the newer version. That is an argument for sending early rather than late — you can keep improving it after the link has gone out, which you cannot do with a forwarded image.

faqs.question: Can I send a Raksha Bandhan wishes link to a sister as well?
faqs.answer: Yes — the mechanics are identical, only the template and the message change. Everything about the sending itself holds: link in its own message, a line of context above it, a password if the contents are private, and a check on a phone before it goes out.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Raksha Bandhan Wishes Link: What Happens After You Send It

A Raksha Bandhan wishes link is a URL you send instead of text — it opens a page you built for one sibling, carrying their name, your photos and your message. It matters because a link gets reopened: SubhSandesh has recorded 36,202 views across 2,973 shared pages, an average of 12.2 opens per page, and 51.1% of those opens happen on a phone.

A forwarded wishes image gets looked at once and buried in a gallery. A link stays in the chat and gets tapped again, sometimes by more than one person. Below: what a link changes, the five things to get right before you send it, who else can see it, and when a link is the wrong call.

## What is a Raksha Bandhan wishes link?

A Raksha Bandhan wishes link is a single web address that opens a personalised greeting page for one recipient. You pick a template, add a name, photos, a message and music, publish it, and you get a URL to paste into WhatsApp.

Nothing gets installed at either end. The page opens in whatever browser is already on the phone, which is the format's real advantage — 51.1% of the 36,202 recorded opens on SubhSandesh happened on a phone rather than a desktop.

It is not the same object as a wishes image. An image is a file that lands in a gallery among a few thousand other forwards, while a link is an address, and an address stays addressable: the same URL still works in November, and every reopen is counted.

## What a link does that a forwarded image cannot

It gets opened more than once. An average of 12.2 opens per page, across 2,973 pages, is the entire argument for the format — one greeting being reopened later, or held up to a parent, or reshared inside the family group.

Now the inconvenient half. Analysing over 35 million public Facebook posts carrying URLs shared between 2017 and 2020, researchers writing in [Nature Human Behaviour found that "shares without clicks" are around 75% of forwarded links](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41562-024-02067-4) (19 November 2024).

Sharing is cheap; opening is not. A link that gets forwarded is not a link that gets read.

A link also refuses to stay one-to-one. Studying WhatsApp use across Barcelona, Groningen and Milan, [Costa and colleagues describe "scalable co-presence" — the way a single WhatsApp thread slides between one-to-one contact and group sociality](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/20563051211069053) (*Social Media + Society*, 2 February 2022). That movement is part of what produces 12.2 opens per page: the URL travels up a scale you did not pick.

So the link is not doing the work on its own. The message you wrap around it is, which is what the next section is about.

## 5 things to get right before you send a Raksha Bandhan wishes link

Each one below follows the same four beats: what it is, why it matters, the number behind it, and what to do.

### 1. Put the link in its own message

Send the URL alone, on its own line, not appended to the end of a paragraph of wishes. A link buried under six lines of text reads as a signature rather than an invitation, and gets treated accordingly.

The Nature Human Behaviour figure is the reason to care: around 75% of forwarded links are shared with nobody clicking them. Write one short message saying what it is, then send the link as the very next message.

### 2. Say what is behind it before they tap

Put a line of context above the link — "made you something for Rakhi, open it when you get a minute". A bare URL dropped into a chat looks like a forward, and forwards are exactly what people scroll past.

On a phone, where 51.1% of opens happen, the preview is a small card that is easy to miss entirely. Name the occasion and name yourself in the line above the link, and never write "click here".

### 3. Password-protect it before you share it

Set the password at publish time, not after the link has already gone out. A URL is a capability: anyone holding it has access, whether you meant them to or not.

The W3C's Technical Architecture Group [recommends such URLs carry an unguessable identifier such as a UUID, and warns they leak through the Referer header, browser history, URL bars and server logs](https://www.w3.org/TR/capability-urls/) (first published 18 February 2014). On SubhSandesh, 44.2% of creators — 1,315 of 2,973 — set a password before sharing, and the password belongs in a separate message from the link.

### 4. Open it on a phone yourself first

Tap your own link on your own phone before it goes anywhere near your brother. You almost certainly built the page on whichever screen you had free; he will open it on the one in his hand, in a browser you did not test.

18,497 of the 36,202 recorded opens — 51.1% — were on a phone. Check the first screen, the photo crop and whether the music autoplays, then send it.

### 5. Finish it the night before, not on the morning

Build and publish a day early and keep the link in your drafts. People keep editing these pages far longer than they plan to: the median gap between a page's first save and its last edit is 6.9 hours, sampled across 931 pages on the /love-gf template.

For Raksha Bandhan on Tuesday 17 August 2027, that means publishing on the Monday evening. 99.4% of started pages do get finished and shared, so the failure mode here is timing rather than nerve.

If you want the scenes already built — the tilak, the aarti thali, the rakhi being tied — the [Raksha Bandhan page for a brother](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-rakshabandhan-to-brother) is the template all of this applies to most directly. It is new and lightly used so far: rakhi templates account for 39 of the 36,202 recorded views, or 0.1%, which is an honest number rather than a flattering one.

## Link, image or screenshot: what actually reaches your brother

Four things people send on Rakhi, compared on what you can verify after it lands.

| What you send | Opens you can count | Needs an app | Can you revoke it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Forwarded wishes image | None — no per-recipient read data exists | No | No |
| Screenshot of a message | None | No | No |
| PDF greeting card | None | Needs a PDF viewer | No |
| A shareable page link | 12.2 average per page (36,202 across 2,973) | No, it opens in the browser | Yes, and 44.2% of creators set a password first |

The link is the only row with a number in the second column. Everything else on that list is sent into the dark, which is fine for a one-line wish to a colleague and a poor choice for something you spent an evening on.

## Who else can see the link once you send it

More people than you are picturing, and not always the person you sent it to. In a study of 199 women across India, Pakistan and Bangladesh, [Sambasivan and colleagues found phones are frequently borrowed and monitored by close social relations — husbands, brothers and parents among them](https://www.usenix.org/conference/soups2018/presentation/sambasivan) (SOUPS, August 2018). The device your sibling opens your link on may not be theirs alone.

That cuts both ways for a Rakhi page. Part of that 12.2 average is a page being held up and shown around, which is usually the point; the part you may not want is an inside joke being read out by an uncle.

A URL also has no expiry of its own, and this is the thing most people get wrong. The W3C guidance is blunt: whoever granted access through a capability URL needs a route to revoke it, because the URL outlives the moment that justified it. Practically, on a Rakhi page, your control is the password rather than the calendar.

## When a Raksha Bandhan wishes link is the wrong choice

Three cases where I would not send one.

If your brother is in the same house, send nothing and tie the rakhi. A link solves distance, and there is no distance here to solve.

If he has no smartphone, or one that labours on the mobile web, the link is a dead end rather than a surprise. The format assumes a browser, which is precisely why 51.1% of opens are phone opens.

And if you want something he will stumble across in five years, the research is against you. In a diary and interview study of 15 adults aged 24 to 66, [van Gennip and colleagues found that physical objects, places and repeated activities cued involuntary memories far more often than digital items and photos did](https://www.materialisingmemories.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/Things_that_make_us_reminisce_CHIv10.pdf) (CHI, April 2015).

A page opened 12 times in a week is not the same as a rakhi in a drawer that catches your eye in 2032. If that is what you are after, send both.

When a link is the right call — a different city, one recipient, something you want reopened rather than scrolled past — you can [browse all SubhSandesh templates](https://subhsandesh.in/templates) and have the URL ready in an evening.

## Sources

- ["Sharing without clicking on news in social media"](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41562-024-02067-4), *Nature Human Behaviour*, 19 November 2024. Paywalled; the 75% figure is taken from the published abstract, which was the only part read.
- Sambasivan et al., ["Privacy is not for me, it's for those rich women": Performative Privacy Practices on Mobile Phones by Women in South Asia](https://www.usenix.org/conference/soups2018/presentation/sambasivan), SOUPS, August 2018. Open access.
- van Gennip, van den Hoven & Markopoulos, ["Things That Make Us Reminisce: Everyday Memory Cues as Opportunities for Interaction Design"](https://www.materialisingmemories.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/04/Things_that_make_us_reminisce_CHIv10.pdf), CHI, 18 April 2015.
- W3C Technical Architecture Group, ["Good Practices for Capability URLs"](https://www.w3.org/TR/capability-urls/), first published 18 February 2014.
- Costa, Esteve-Del-Valle & Hagedoorn, ["Scalable Co-presence: WhatsApp and the Mediation of Personal Relationships during the COVID-19 Lockdown"](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/20563051211069053), *Social Media + Society*, 2 February 2022. Open access, CC BY 4.0.
- First-party figures throughout come from SubhSandesh's own database, measured 25 August 2026.

failed.why: Seven first-party facts are used and four sit in the first 150 words, so the count is met — but every one of them is platform-wide rather than keyword-specific, which the batch brief requires be recorded as a failure. `rakshabandhanpages` holds 3 documents and rakhi templates account for 39 of 36,202 recorded views (0.1%), so no rate, percentage or 'most creators' claim was computed from rakhi data; the post states plainly that the template is new and lightly used. The 12.2-opens, 51.1%-mobile and 44.2%-password figures genuinely describe link behaviour, which is a closer fit to this keyword than to most in the batch, but they are evidence about SubhSandesh pages, not about Raksha Bandhan. Closes when rakhi template usage passes roughly 500 pages; re-query then.

failed.why: Five outbound links; three were fetched directly and read in full — the W3C document (unguessable UUID, Referer/browser-history leakage, the granter's need to revoke), the SOUPS 2018 PDF (199 women in India, Pakistan and Bangladesh; phones borrowed and monitored by husbands and brothers) and the CHI 2015 PDF (15 adults aged 24–66; digital items less frequent memory cues than physical objects). Two publishers return 403 to any automated request: nature.com, whose 75% figure was verified against the published abstract via PubMed (PMID 39562798), and journals.sagepub.com, whose 'scalable co-presence' claim and CC BY 4.0 licence were verified via Crossref and OpenAlex. Both claims are verified and cite only what the abstract states; the linked pages are not themselves the artefacts that verified them. Closes if author manuscripts reach open repositories.

When 6 sibling files had landed, arxiv.org was already at 6 posts — double the domain cap — so the arXiv WhatsApp source originally used here was dropped and replaced with Costa et al. in Social Media + Society (journals.sagepub.com, CC BY 4.0), which is peer-reviewed, gold open access, and a better fit for the one-to-one-to-group point it supports. After the swap all five of this post's URLs and all five domains (nature.com, usenix.org, materialisingmemories.com, w3.org, journals.sagepub.com) are at count 1 across every sibling file visible. Three of the 47 posts were still unwritten at that moment, so the final count is the orchestrator's to make.

auditReport.honestAssessment: Six of six pages on this SERP contain the string 'shareable link' exactly zero times and cite no statistic at all, so this is the only page that answers the mechanical question the query actually asks — what happens after you send the link — and the only one carrying verified numbers (12.2 opens per page, 51.1% mobile, 44.2% password-protected) alongside a W3C capability-URL argument and a CHI finding that runs against its own recommendation. What it cannot overcome: subhsandesh.in has far less authority than Adobe, FNP or CaratLane, and every first-party number is platform-wide rather than rakhi-specific, so an answer engine gets a genuinely distinct source on link behaviour but not on Raksha Bandhan itself.
